claims.statement: A full-rank linear intertwiner from the incidence/B-L source plane to the exchange-even/odd Furey face plane exists only if the source plane carries one even and one odd reversal line.
dependencies: source and target are real two-dimensional label spaces
target face exchange has eigenvalues +1 and -1
the map is linear and exchange equivariant
claims.falsifier: Exhibit an invertible solution of C_F M = M C_S when C_S is +I or -I.

claims.statement: Fixing the B-L line to the exchange-even face sum and matching the established free-UV Gram matrix leaves two source-to-face isometries related by reversal of the face-difference orientation.
dependencies: free-UV Gram matrix [[231,9],[9,48]]
Euclidean normalization of the face exchange eigenbasis
positive orientation fixed on the B-L image
claims.falsifier: Find a third metric-matched map satisfying the same Ward-axis condition that is not one of the two orientation reversals.

claims.statement: The bare incidence and B-L vector-current pair does not currently supply the relative odd source-label line required to identify physical CP/reversal with Furey face exchange.
dependencies: the shared Lorentz transformation is factored from the current-label action
no additional CP-odd spurion or boundary orientation is assumed
claims.falsifier: Derive from the same Standard-Model action a gauge-invariant renormalized odd source direction that pairs with the protected even B-L line.

claims.statement: Natural KO-6 reality and relation composition generate a dihedral D3 action, not a Mobius C6 transport.
dependencies: r has order three
J has order two
J r J = r inverse
claims.falsifier: Construct an order-six element inside the permutation action satisfying those three relations.

claims.statement: A direct relation reversal is first-order forbidden, while a shortest off-diagonal one-spectator resolution uses three elementary first-order edges and two one-sided spectator sectors.
dependencies: strict first-order rook rule
diagonal loop sectors excluded
one added spectator character S
claims.falsifier: Exhibit a direct or two-edge off-diagonal first-order path from (i,j) to (j,i), with i not equal to j, under the same vertex contract.

claims.statement: One spectator character cannot mediate all three relation reversals with a cyclically symmetric wholly grading-odd Dirac graph because the required one-sided mediator sectors form an odd triangle.
dependencies: all three reversal paths use the same spectator S
every elementary Dirac edge is grading odd
cyclic completion retains all three middle edges
claims.falsifier: Give a two-coloring of the PS-NS-IS triangle or a cyclic completion avoiding that triangle under the same one-spectator contract.

claims.statement: One selected length-three mediated seam remains graphically viable, but its Mobius transport is physical only if the composite survives junk while its anchor-mixing scalar projection vanishes non-accidentally.
dependencies: an explicit finite spectral datum (A_F,H_F,pi,D_F,gamma,J)
represented products through degree three
a computed junk quotient and kinetic projection
claims.falsifier: The composite is junk, or every nonzero surviving composite necessarily induces the forbidden anchor-mixing scalar.

claims.statement: Reality closure of one shortest mediated reversal path gives an explicit six-sector C6 Dirac graph satisfying the label-level KO-6, grading, order-zero and strict first-order conditions.
dependencies: finite label algebra with characters P, N and S
six sectors PN, PS, NS, NP, SP and SN
equal nonzero real edge weights in the minimal witness
claims.falsifier: Find a failed KO-6 sign or a nonzero double commutator [[D,L(a)],R(b)] in the displayed six-sector matrices.

claims.statement: The one-seam half-turn is a nonzero alternating opposite-left-opposite product but is not represented in either ordinary left or ordinary opposite degree-three universal calculus.
dependencies: ordinary single-algebra Connes differential envelope
the explicit six-sector C6 witness
separate left and opposite representations
claims.falsifier: Express E(PN,NP) as a represented element of ordinary Omega_D^3(A) or Omega_D^3(A-op) for the displayed witness.

claims.statement: In the maximal joint diagonal six-point Connes calculus, the represented degree-three image equals degree-three junk and the mediated seam E(PN,NP) has an explicit junk preimage.
dependencies: the joint left/right image is promoted to the full diagonal C^6 algebra
the equal-weight C6 Dirac witness
the standard Connes junk quotient
claims.falsifier: Show that the explicit preimage is not in ker(pi_2), that its differential is not E(PN,NP), or that E(PN,NP) survives the stated quotient.

claims.statement: Physical survival of the mediated Mobius seam is indeterminate until a mixed bimodule differential calculus or superconnection, including its degree-three junk ideal and action, is declared.
dependencies: a bigraded calculus containing alternating right-left-right products
a differential and junk ideal compatible with J and gamma
a gauge-covariant action distinguishing transport from a physical anchor-mixing scalar
claims.falsifier: Prove that every admissible mixed calculus kills the seam or construct one independently motivated calculus in which the seam survives with a protected coefficient and no anchor leakage.

claims.statement: In every associative matrix representation retaining the three elementary seam edges, their mixed product is exactly the forbidden endpoint operator E(PN,NP); a projection killing anchor mixing also kills the represented seam.
dependencies: the explicit rank-one elementary matrix units
associative composition in End(H)
anchor projectors P_PN and P_NP
claims.falsifier: Construct a nonzero represented component of the elementary-edge product outside the PN-to-NP anchor block without enlarging the representation.

claims.statement: The same left/right degree-one module admits a free mixed completion retaining the seam and a differential-ideal quotient killing it, so current module and KO data do not determine mixed degree three.
dependencies: only the represented degree-one bimodules are fixed
no mixed universality or junk prescription is imposed
claims.falsifier: Derive from the existing finite module a universal property that uniquely selects one of the two mixed completions.

claims.statement: For the minimal KO-real C6 witness, the open half-holonomy has the forbidden endpoint gauge type, while the closed Wilson product is |abc|^2 and is orientation even.
dependencies: JD=DJ pairs second-half weights with first-half conjugates
the minimal single C6 path
ordinary endpoint gauge covariance
claims.falsifier: Produce a gauge-invariant orientation-odd phase from the same single KO-real six-cycle without adding a second path or central phase datum.

claims.statement: A physical Mobius seam now requires an independently motivated enriched transport representation, central extension, higher-categorical lift, boundary endpoint interpretation or protected two-path interference observable.
dependencies: new structure beyond the current finite matter module
a derivation of its action and quotient
a gauge-invariant orientation-sensitive observable
claims.falsifier: Either construct such a derived extension with a protected observable, or prove that every admissible extension reduces to anchor mixing or orientation-even closed holonomy.

claims.statement: The established Peirce H2(R) module is three-dimensional but, with the currently trivial topology action on W_mediator, every O(2)-equivariant map to W has rank at most one and its image line remains arbitrary in CP2.
dependencies: H2(R)=1 plus the two-dimensional traceless O(2) module
no derived O(2) action on W_mediator
the independent U(3) mediator commutant
claims.falsifier: Derive a nontrivial O(2) action on W and a full-rank normalized intertwiner from existing Peirce data without importing a Clebsch row or target line.

claims.statement: The three-label ribbon/permutation module has a two-dimensional invariant endomorphism algebra, so symmetry permits a singlet-doublet anisotropy but does not normalize it; the natural Walsh metric is scalar.
dependencies: the S3 permutation representation decomposes as 1 plus 2
equal atomic or Walsh weighting
no Standard-Model-typed handle exchange acting on mediator copies
claims.falsifier: Derive from the ribbon action a unique non-unit singlet/doublet Gram ratio and the corresponding typed action on W_mediator.

claims.statement: The intrinsic Golay M11 ordered-point flag does not canonically produce a normalized positive real three-module: rank three first occurs after choosing three ordered points, over F3, with a three-dimensional invariant-form space.
dependencies: the established five-dimensional characteristic-three Golay carrier
the sharply four-transitive M11 ordered-point stabilizer chain
no independently selected integral real lift
claims.falsifier: Construct an intrinsic flag-free rank-three real positive quotient with a unique form and a typed equivariant map to W_mediator.

claims.statement: Spin_0(2,3) has no nontrivial three-dimensional linear representation; an H2(R) linear section of its five-vector instead lies in a six-dimensional embedding orbit with setwise stabilizer SO_0(1,2) times SO_0(1,1).
dependencies: simplicity and dimension ten of sp4(R)
dimension nine of gl3(R)
the signature-(1,2) section theorem in the five-dimensional vector module
claims.falsifier: Exhibit a nontrivial Lie-algebra homomorphism sp4(R) to gl3(R), or show that the stated section stabilizer has dimension other than four.

claims.statement: The first missing W4-C datum is a physically typed nontrivial source-symmetry representation on W_mediator, derived without q_QQ, together with a normalized equivariant pairing that fixes the singlet-doublet relative scale and selects one incidence ray.
dependencies: a named source symmetry from Peirce, ribbon, code or a broken Spin(2,3) subgroup
an independently derived action rho_W on the mediator copies
counterterm and heavy-threshold stability
claims.falsifier: Either construct the normalized cross-carrier action and show uniqueness up to overall phase, or prove that every admissible action retains a transitive target commutant or a free Gram ratio.
